commits.author: Patrick Baumgartner
commits.message:
Document the project and add community health files

README with screenshots from the live deployment, architecture and
module map, the zero-JavaScript rule, build and test instructions,
station and artwork provenance, and Web Image's current limits stated
plainly. Changelog, contributing guide, security policy, code of
conduct, and issue and pull request templates.

commits.author: Patrick Baumgartner
commits.message:
Automate verification and delivery

CI validates formatting and the JVM suite, builds the container from
scratch, runs the browser and smoke tests against the image, and - on
every push to main - deploys the exact tested site to GitHub Pages and
publishes the exact tested image to Docker Hub. CodeQL, dependency
review and Dependabot watch the dependencies.

commits.author: Patrick Baumgartner
commits.message:
Serve from an unprivileged nginx container

A two-stage build: the first stage pins and checksum-verifies Oracle
GraalVM and Binaryen, compiles the module with -Os, shrinks it further
with wasm-opt -Oz and precompresses every compressible asset at
gzip -9; the runtime stage is unprivileged nginx serving static files
only - no JVM, no jar. gzip_static delivers the 16 MB module as
6.8 MB on the wire, with security headers, immutable caching and a
health endpoint.

commits.author: Patrick Baumgartner
commits.message:
Add the JVM and browser test suites

Everything that can be proven without a browser is: unit tests for the
player state machine, persistence, and both catalogues, a Spring
context test per module boundary, Spring Modulith verification, Taikai
architecture conventions, and the zero-JavaScript constraint. The
authoritative layer drives the built module in real Chromium via
Playwright - real playback, reload persistence, keyboard media
controls, breakpoint reachability - and DockerSmokeTests asserts what
the container serves: content types, immutable caching, compressed
delivery, security headers, and the absence of any JVM or jar.

commits.author: Patrick Baumgartner
commits.message:
myTunes: a complete Spring Boot application compiled to WebAssembly

A radio player whose framework, domain and user interface are Java,
compiled ahead of time by GraalVM Web Image and executed entirely in
the browser. Spring Boot 4.1.1 and Spring Modulith 2.1.0 boot in the
tab in ~140 ms with 22 beans; the interface is built against the live
DOM through a two-expression interop surface, and the repository
contains no hand-written JavaScript.

The station catalogue holds eight categories with 30 channels: every
category leads with an audio loop generated by tools/generate-audio.py
and served with the application, the rest are live streams from SomaFM,
Nightride FM and Radio Paradise, each verified to answer browsers with
an audio content type and permissive CORS (tools/generate-stations.py
re-runs that verification). The five animated landscape backgrounds are
generated SVG scenes (tools/generate-artwork.py) with a declarative
SMIL day-night cycle. Preferences persist in localStorage behind a
versioned schema; Media Session and a Document Picture-in-Picture mini
player are feature-detected.
